newsitem.title: USA: U.S. military stops border patrols after killing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. military stops border patrols after killing.

text.p: Military patrols along the U.S.-Mexico border in the Big Bend area of Texas were suspended on Thursday after a Marine shot dead a high school student in a disputed incident earlier this week.
Border Patrol spokesman Mario Ortiz said Task Force Six, a military agency that helps civilian authorities in anti-drugs efforts along the border, was pulling back from the remote area.

"The Border Patrol and Task Force Six are suspending all military operations on the border so that something like this doesn't happen again," Ortiz said in a telephone interview at Border Patrol offices in the west Texas town of Marfa.
But military operations along the rest of the border would continue, officials said.
Ezequiel Hernandez, 18, was shot dead by a Marine on Tuesday near his home in the Big Bend, an isolated mountainous area popular among drug traffickers as well as hikers and tourists.

Family members said Hernandez was tending a herd of goats when he was shot but Ortiz said the teenager had opened fire with a .22 calibre rifle on a four-person team of Marines armed with M-16 rifles.
"That area is notorious for alien and drug trafficking, but we don't know why he would fire at a group of Marines," Ortiz said.
Hernandez' sister Belen said she did not believe he fired on the Marines.

Maureen Bossch, a spokeswoman for Task Force Six, said the incident was being investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Texas Department of Public Safety and local law enforcement officials.
Task Force Six has about 150 active-duty and reserve members taken from the Navy, Army, Marine Corps and Air Force.
A unit from the agency was in the second week of a planned three-week deployment in the Big Bend area when Hernandez was killed.
